indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B4.5.1.1 Recognise the importance of personal hygiene
indicator.objective: Know how to care for one's self and the environment

skills.description: Name personal hygiene practices (bathing, brushing teeth, cutting nails, washing clothes/towels).
Explain simply why each hygiene practice matters (e.g. bathing removes dirt and germs, brushing prevents tooth decay).
State what can happen if personal hygiene is neglected (body odour, sickness, germs).
Identify materials used for hygiene (soap, toothbrush, toothpaste, water, nail cutter, towel).
Give examples of caring for the environment (sweeping classroom, disposing of waste properly).
Describe a simple daily hygiene routine (e.g. bath twice daily, brush teeth morning and night).

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: Bathing once a week is enough.
Brushing teeth once a day is enough.
Dirty fingernails are not a health problem.
Personal hygiene is only about looking good.
Sweeping the classroom is not part of hygiene.

questions.stem: Which of these is a personal hygiene practice?
hints: Which activity keeps your body clean?
It involves soap and water.
questions.explanation: Bathing regularly is a personal hygiene practice. It removes dirt and germs from the body.
questions.misconception: Personal hygiene is only about looking good.

questions.stem: Which materials are used for brushing teeth?
hints: You use them in your mouth.
They help keep teeth clean.
questions.explanation: A toothbrush and toothpaste are used for brushing teeth. They help remove food particles and prevent tooth decay.
questions.misconception: Brushing teeth once a day is enough.

questions.stem: Why do we bathe?
hints: What does soap and water remove?
Dirt and germs collect on the body.
questions.explanation: We bathe to remove dirt and germs from our bodies. This helps us stay clean and healthy.
questions.misconception: Bathing is only for looking good.

questions.stem: How often should you brush your teeth?
options: Twice a day, morning and night
hints: Think about morning and before bed.
Brushing twice a day keeps teeth healthy.
questions.explanation: You should brush your teeth twice a day, in the morning and before going to bed, to keep them clean and healthy.
questions.misconception: Brushing teeth once a day is enough.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a personal hygiene practice?
hints: Which activity makes you dirty?
Hygiene practices keep you clean.
questions.explanation: Playing in the mud is not a hygiene practice; it makes you dirty. Washing hands, cutting nails and bathing are hygiene practices.
questions.misconception: Any activity is a hygiene practice.

questions.stem: Why should you cut your fingernails?
options: To keep dirt and germs out
hints: Dirt can hide under long nails.
Short nails are easier to keep clean.
questions.explanation: Cutting fingernails keeps dirt and germs from collecting under them, which helps prevent sickness.
questions.misconception: Dirty fingernails are not a health problem.

questions.stem: What can happen if you do not bathe regularly?
hints: What happens when sweat stays on the body?
It can cause an unpleasant smell.
questions.explanation: If you do not bathe regularly, sweat and dirt collect on the body, causing body odour.
questions.misconception: Bathing once a week is enough.

questions.stem: Which materials are used to clean the armpit?
hints: What do you use in the bathroom?
Soap helps remove dirt and smell.
questions.explanation: Soap and water are used to clean the armpit. They remove dirt and sweat that cause body odour.
questions.misconception: Water alone is enough to clean the armpit.

questions.stem: Which materials are used to wash clothes?
hints: What do you use in a washing basin?
Soap removes dirt from cloth.
questions.explanation: Soap and water are used to wash clothes. They remove dirt and make the clothes clean.
questions.misconception: Washing clothes does not need soap.

questions.stem: What is a good daily hygiene routine?
options: Bathe twice daily and brush teeth morning and night
hints: Think about morning and evening activities.
Good routines include bathing and brushing.
questions.explanation: A good daily routine includes bathing twice a day and brushing teeth morning and night. This keeps the body clean and healthy.
questions.misconception: Bathing once a week is enough.

questions.stem: Which of these is a hygiene practice at school?
hints: Which activity keeps the classroom clean?
It involves a broom.
questions.explanation: Sweeping the classroom is a hygiene practice at school. It keeps the learning environment clean and free from dirt.
questions.misconception: Sweeping the classroom is not part of hygiene.

questions.stem: Why should you wash your towels regularly?
hints: Towels collect sweat and dirt.
Washing removes germs.
questions.explanation: Washing towels regularly removes dirt and germs that collect on them. This helps prevent skin infections and sickness.
questions.misconception: Washing towels is not necessary.

questions.stem: What can happen if you do not cut your fingernails?
options: Dirt and germs can collect under them and make you sick
Your nails will turn to gold
hints: Long nails can trap dirt.
Dirt under nails can enter your mouth.
questions.explanation: If you do not cut your fingernails, dirt and germs collect under them. These can enter your body when you eat, making you sick.
questions.misconception: Dirty fingernails are not a health problem.

questions.stem: Why should you sweep your classroom?
options: To keep it clean and free from dirt
hints: What does sweeping remove?
A clean classroom is good for learning.
questions.explanation: Sweeping the classroom keeps it clean and free from dirt. This helps create a healthy learning environment.
questions.misconception: Sweeping the classroom is not part of hygiene.

questions.stem: What is a good routine for washing clothes?
options: Wash clothes regularly with soap and water
Wear dirty clothes until they smell
hints: Dirty clothes can cause skin problems.
Regular washing keeps clothes clean.
questions.explanation: A good routine is to wash clothes regularly with soap and water. This removes dirt and germs and keeps the body healthy.
questions.misconception: Washing clothes is not necessary.

questions.stem: Why is personal hygiene important?
options: It helps prevent sickness and keeps you healthy
hints: Germs cause sickness.
Hygiene removes germs.
questions.explanation: Personal hygiene is important because it removes germs and dirt, helping to prevent sickness and keep you healthy.
questions.misconception: Personal hygiene is only about looking good.

questions.stem: How can learners care for the school environment?
hints: Where should waste go?
Bins keep the environment clean.
questions.explanation: Learners can care for the school environment by throwing waste into bins. This keeps the compound clean and healthy.
questions.misconception: Littering is acceptable.

questions.stem: Explain why poor hygiene can cause sickness.
answer: because germs from dirt can enter the body and cause diseases
germs collect on dirty bodies and can make you sick
poor hygiene allows germs to spread and cause illness
hints: Think about germs on dirty hands.
Germs can enter the mouth.
questions.explanation: Poor hygiene allows germs to collect on the body and hands. These germs can enter the body through the mouth or skin and cause sickness.
questions.misconception: Personal hygiene is only about looking good.

questions.stem: Which set lists only personal hygiene practices?
hints: Which set keeps the body clean?
Hygiene practices involve soap, water and cleanliness.
questions.explanation: Bathing, brushing teeth and cutting nails are all personal hygiene practices. The other sets are not about hygiene.
questions.misconception: Any activity is a hygiene practice.

questions.stem: Why is caring for the environment part of personal hygiene?
answer: because a clean environment helps prevent sickness and keeps people healthy
a dirty environment breeds germs that make people sick
keeping the environment clean reduces diseases
hints: Dirty surroundings attract germs.
Clean surroundings keep you healthy.
questions.explanation: Caring for the environment is part of personal hygiene because a clean environment reduces germs and helps prevent sickness, keeping people healthy.
questions.misconception: Sweeping the classroom is not part of hygiene.
